mysteries.title: Fragment of the Red Tower
mysteries.posterText: A Forgotten Order scholar will pay handsomely for a confirmed Fragment of the Red Tower — the cursed Etheric core's outer casing, never recovered intact. 400 TC.

stages.narration: The scholar slides a sketch across the table — a hexagonal Tartarian ironwork, the seal of Nimari embossed into one face. "The Red Tower's outer ring shed pieces when it cooled. They turn up. Find one."

You think back through old salvage notes. Nimari, Red Tower, Etheric core. Reclaimers say the fragments roll downhill — anywhere mud collects, eventually one ends up. Mudstone-rich ground is the place to look.
stages.arbiter: "You know the where," the Arbiter says. "Now do the work."

stages.narration: You dig along a Mudstone vein where the silt has built up a lip. After an hour, a piece of the casing catches your blade — hexagonal, faintly warm to the touch.
You wipe the casing clean. The seal of Nimari is intact. This will satisfy the scholar.
stages.arbiter: "That fragment is centuries old," the Arbiter says. "It remembers the Tower. Carry it carefully."

mysteries.title: Cradle of Dusk Compass
mysteries.posterText: Halem the Trader offers 300 TC for a working Cradle of Dusk Compass — one of the few instruments that holds steady in Aetheric storms.

stages.narration: Halem unrolls a worn map of the Mud Seas, taps the Cradle of Dusk. "Old Tartarian surveying instrument. Brass face, three needles. Anyone who sails the Mud Seas wants one. Bring me a working piece."

You make your way to the Cradle's edge. The wreckage of an old surveying vessel sits half-glassed in the haze. Inside, a Tartarian instrument console — and one of the compasses still intact in its bracket.
stages.arbiter: "They never abandoned this place willingly," the Arbiter says. "Take what is still here to take."

stages.narration: You pry the compass free. The three needles snap to attention immediately, aligned with currents you cannot feel. Halem will pay for this without bargaining.

mysteries.title: The Leviathan's Eye
mysteries.posterText: True Tartarian agents will pay 500 TC and faith-favor for the preserved eye of a Mud Seas Leviathan — said to see through Etheric storms.

stages.narration: The True Tartarian agent meets you in the dark. "Leviathan, Mud Seas. Old beast. It died long ago, but its eye does not rot in Aetherstone — find the carcass, take the eye, bring it here."
stages.arbiter: "Bones of leviathans show up in the most unflattering places," the Arbiter says. "Look where the Seas have receded."

stages.narration: You walk the receding edge of the Mud Seas. The Leviathan's spine breaks the surface like a ridge of ribbed stone — long dead, every scale fossilised.
You climb the spine to where the skull lies submerged. The eye-socket is the size of a window. You reach in — the eye is still there, fossilised but intact, the size of a melon.
stages.arbiter: "The leviathans were watching the storms before there were Tartarians," the Arbiter says.

stages.narration: You wrap the eye in your pack and back away from the carcass. The Mud Seas resettle behind you — the only witness is the haze.

mysteries.title: Temporal Distortion Watch
mysteries.posterText: Reclaimers Guild Speaker pays 600 TC and will move you up the haul board for a working Temporal Distortion Watch — Tartarian-make, useful in deep ruins.

stages.narration: The Speaker spreads the contract. "Watch — Tartarian make, hexagonal face, three dials. Counts the way the local Etheric time bends. Reclaimers used to wear them. Find a working one."
Old Reclaimer wisdom: the watches turn up in preserved corpses — anyone who died in a temporal eddy got their watch fossilised with them. You head into the eddies.
stages.arbiter: "Time bent backward for these people," the Arbiter says. "Their gear bent with them."

stages.narration: You find a Reclaimer body in an eddy zone — perfectly preserved, the watch still on the wrist, ticking in slow waves.
You unstrap the watch. The dials settle into normal time as you leave the eddy. The Speaker will pay without question.

mysteries.title: Shifting Obsidian Orb
mysteries.posterText: Mud Monarch courier offers 700 TC for a Shifting Obsidian Orb — an Obsidian Pillar fragment fused with Aetherstone. Reshapes itself.

stages.narration: The courier is well-dressed and brief. "Obsidian Pillars. The Orbs only form where one of the pillars cracks under an Aetheric storm. Find a recently-storm-struck pillar. Recover the Orb."
stages.arbiter: "Mud Monarchs do not pay seven hundred TC for nothing," the Arbiter says. "Make sure you know what you carry."

stages.narration: You find a pillar with fresh damage — Aetheric scoring along one face. The Orb has rolled into the silt at its base. Black as obsidian, but it does not hold a single shape.
You pick the Orb out of the silt. It is heavy in a way that changes — sometimes a stone's weight, sometimes a feather's.
You secure the Orb. The courier's coin is good. Whatever the Monarchs want it for is their concern, not yours — yet.
stages.arbiter: "You may meet this Orb again," the Arbiter says. "In other hands."
